relationships.subject: Nav1.8 G1662S
relationships.evidence_quote: dynamic clamp introduction of the Nav1.8WT/GS model in small DRG neurons produced pro-electrogenic effects on the generation of repetitive AP firing

relationships.subject: Nav1.8
relationships.evidence_quote: Repetitive AP firing of primary nociceptive neurons is driven by Nav1.8 (Renganathan et al., 2001)

key_findings: The Nav1.8 G1662S gain-of-function mutation does not change rheobase, RMP or single AP threshold but nearly doubles APs during repetitive firing in small DRG neurons (dynamic clamp).
Hyperexcitability is attributed to enhanced suprathreshold sodium charge, depolarized steady-state inactivation and accelerated recovery from inactivation.
